newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican guerrillas surrounded, expect more fighting.
newsitem.headline: Mexican guerrillas surrounded, expect more fighting.

text.p: Hundreds of Mexican troops were to resume searching the rugged mountains of Mexico's state of Guerrero on Thursday, continuing a search for Marxist rebels who killed three soldiers.
Late on Wednesday, a rebel statement said that some of its guerrillas were surrounded and more fighting was imminent. No further details were given.

On Wednesday, helicopter gunships and small aircraft flew overhead as combat troops fanned out across the Pacific coast region, which lies between the resort cities of Acapulco and Ixtapa, about 150 miles (250 km) southwest of Mexico City.
Armoured personnel carriers rumbled along the dusty roads, machineguns at the ready. Jeeps, one bearing bulletholes and one stained with blood at the rear, followed behind.
Rifle-toting troops prevented reporters from reaching the scene of Tuesday's attacks by the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), the group's second armed strike in four days.
In Acapulco, the rebels released a statement saying some of their fighters were surrounded by government troops in western Mexico and that more fighting was imminent.
The rebels also said in a statement that EPR leaders suspected that two rebels were captured in a firefight with soldiers last Saturday and were being tortured.
The Mexican army has refused to confirm that any prisoners were taken during encounters Saturday and Tuesday.

Five soldiers and four rebels have been confirmed killed in the two battles. However the rebels claim to have killed or wounded as many as 30 soldiers in Saturday's fighting about 60 miles (100 km) east of the Guerrero state capital of Chilpancingo.
The statement was signed by Commander Hermeneglido.
Earlier Wednesday, a military source said that Hermeneglido had been captured during one of the battles Tuesday.

The local military command said three soldiers and two unidentified gunmen were killed in Tuesday's incidents, which took place in the town of Atoyac de Alvarez, some 40 miles (62 km) northwest of Acapulco.

In Mexico City, federal officials did their best to play down the attacks. The Defence Ministry, the Interior Ministry and the presidency all either failed to take calls or said they had no information about the incident beyond the 11-line army statement issued Tuesday.
In the town of Atoyac, reporters saw the bodies of two men brought to a morgue wearing olive green uniforms with bandannas round their necks and military boots.

"Their uniforms don't have anything that explicitly states EPR on them. But we presume from their uniforms, their boots, their weapons and the covering of their faces, everything indicates they are members of the EPR", said Efrain Mendoza Ortiz, a local prosecutor investigating the incident.
The Marxist EPR, which first appeared in the state at the end of June 1996 calling for the overthrow of President Ernesto Zedillo's government.
